reels.label: Instagram Reels
reels.notes: 15 min / 300 MB / H.264 / 23-60 fps / 25 Mbps VBR max / AAC 128 kbps from the Graph API Reels spec (the tighter figure; help.instagram.com/2720958398006062 says 20 min in app). Reels over 3 min are not recommended to new audiences. Safe zone is Meta's Reels ads guidance (14% top, 35% bottom, 6% sides) at https://www.facebook.com/business/help/980593475366490/ . Estimated: lufs/truePeak are the common social default (-14 LUFS, -1 dBTP); the platform publishes no loudness target.

tiktok.label: TikTok
tiktok.notes: 10 min / 4 GB / H.264 recommended / 23-60 fps from TikTok's Content Posting API guide; most creators default to 3 min in app. Estimated: safe (TikTok publishes only downloadable overlay PNGs, margins from common creator guidance: caption + action rail); lufs/truePeak are the common social default (-14 LUFS, -1 dBTP); the platform publishes no loudness target.

shorts.label: YouTube Shorts
shorts.notes: Shorts are square or vertical and up to 3 min. No practical file cap (general YouTube upload limit is far above any Short). Encoding per https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/1722171 (H.264 High, 12 Mbps at 1080p 48-60 fps, AAC-LC 48 kHz). Estimated: safe (Google publishes template PNGs only; margins from creator guidance for title/channel and action rail); lufs/truePeak are the common social default (-14 LUFS, -1 dBTP); the platform publishes no loudness target.

x.label: X (square)
x.notes: 140 s / 512 MB for non-Premium accounts (Premium is longer and larger: https://help.x.com/en/using-x/premium-longer-videos). Direct fetch returned 403; figures taken from search results quoting the official page. Estimated: safe (feed shows the full frame without overlays); lufs/truePeak are the common social default (-14 LUFS, -1 dBTP); the platform publishes no loudness target.

x-landscape.label: X (landscape)
x-landscape.notes: Same limits as x: 140 s / 512 MB non-Premium; direct fetch returned 403, figures from search results quoting the official page. Estimated: safe (no overlays in feed); lufs/truePeak are the common social default (-14 LUFS, -1 dBTP); the platform publishes no loudness target.

linkedin.label: LinkedIn (square)
linkedin.notes: LinkedIn Pages spec: 3 s to 10 min, 75 KB to 5 GB, 10-60 fps, 192 kbps to 30 Mbps, MP4/H.264 (MOV no longer supported). Third-party guides cite 15 min for member desktop uploads; 10 min is the official conservative figure. Estimated: safe (feed shows the full frame); lufs/truePeak are the common social default (-14 LUFS, -1 dBTP); the platform publishes no loudness target.

linkedin-landscape.label: LinkedIn (landscape)
linkedin-landscape.notes: Same limits as linkedin: 10 min / 5 GB per the LinkedIn Pages video spec. Estimated: safe (feed shows the full frame); lufs/truePeak are the common social default (-14 LUFS, -1 dBTP); the platform publishes no loudness target.

discord.label: Discord
discord.notes: Free upload limit is 20 MB as of August 2026 (up from 10 MB), checked before compression on all platforms; Nitro Basic 50 MB. Direct fetch returned 403; figures from search results quoting the official page. The plan assumed 10 MB. Estimated: safe (inline player, no overlays); lufs/truePeak are the common social default (-14 LUFS, -1 dBTP); the platform publishes no loudness target.

discord-nitro.label: Discord (Nitro)
discord-nitro.notes: Nitro upload limit is 1 GB per the official File Attachments FAQ (the 500 MB to 1 GB change Jack mentioned has landed); stored as 1000 MB so it is under the cap however GB is counted. Direct fetch returned 403; figures from search results quoting the official page. Estimated: safe; lufs/truePeak are the common social default (-14 LUFS, -1 dBTP); the platform publishes no loudness target.

web.label: Web / wiki / GitHub
web.notes: No platform limits: small faststart MP4 (H.264/AAC) plus WebM (VP9/Opus) plus poster JPG for self-hosted pages. Public because wiki/GitHub pages are public-facing. Quality and loudness are house defaults.

gif.label: GIF (README)
gif.notes: Palette GIF for READMEs. 10 MB cap follows the commonly cited GitHub image upload limit (not officially confirmed here); width 720 and 15 fps are house defaults. video block describes the intermediate render only; the GIF has no audio.
